title: Fisheye Warping
subtitle: Fisheye Image Processing Tool
description: Unrolls top-down fisheye images into panoramas and rolls them back again, so nobody has to squint at round photos.
longDescription: An OpenCV Python package and CLI that dewarps top-down fisheye images into panoramas and rewarps panoramas into fisheye circles. Coordinate meshes are cached by image size so repeated conversions can reuse the mapping.
why: At Infortrend, pose recognition ran on top-down fisheye cameras in narrow spaces, and this was the step before it: unrolling the round frame into a panorama. Working out where each pixel goes is slow, so it is done once per image size and saved, on the safe bet that the camera won't change resolution by itself.
gains: Ceiling cameras, 360° cameras pointed up or down and tiny-planet photos become flat panoramas, and panoramas can be wrapped back into circles. After one mesh per resolution, each frame takes well under a second, even on a server or in a slim Docker image.
lessons: Mesh cost grows with the pixel count: 1024 × 1024 takes 4 s and 0.5 GB on 32 cores, so a 4096 × 4096 image would need about 8 GB.
The centre pixel of a rewarped image is always black: the angle at the exact centre is undefined, and no amount of maths will pick one.
Up to 1.0.2, running the command with options missing still exited with 0, success; it now exits with 2 and prints the usage line.
